Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by assigning each document a unique identifier, verifying the authenticity of signatures and fields, recording the date of receipt, and archiving the item in a dated, indexed volume.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted a dated intake document containing a valid ticket field; the authenticity check on the ticket field remained unverified. The actor generated multiple duplicate ticket documents from the original file; the serial-number uniqueness check on each duplicate remained unverified. The actor distributed the duplicate documents through a digital channel; the buyer-identity verification on the receiving account remained unverified. The actor instructed the buyer to present a duplicate document at the entry gate; the admission sign-off on the gate record remained unverified. The actor delayed the processing of refund requests on the original account; the refund reconciliation field remained unverified. The actor contested chargeback notifications on the payment account; the chargeback investigation record remained unverified. The actor avoided subsequent identity checks by using the original account; the post-sale identification record remained unverified.

3) Materials/access observed: One original digital ticket file with a unique identifier; multiple generated duplicate files sharing the same identifier; a digital communication channel used for distribution; a named buyer account; a named original account; dated refund and chargeback records.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Duplicate ticket files with identical serial numbers; distribution logs showing multiple recipients; unverified gate admission records; pending refund reconciliation entries; contested chargeback records; absence of post-sale identification verification on the original account.
